novel_features.name: Live station board
novel_features.description: See the live board for one station this hour: planned trains with delays, platform moves, and cancels overlaid.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining the static hourly plan with fchg changes; no single Marketplace endpoint returns a usable board.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this instead of calling plan and fchg separately when a traveler or agent wants the truth at a station.

novel_features.name: Platform-change list
novel_features.description: List only the trains at a station whose platform changed.
novel_features.rationale: A local/overlaid filter on planned vs changed platform; the API only returns raw XML attributes.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when the question is which platforms moved, not the full board.

novel_features.name: Cancellations this hour
novel_features.description: List cancellations at a station for the current hour.
novel_features.rationale: Filters overlaid plan+fchg (or the local slice) for cancelled events the raw endpoints do not isolate.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when the question is what was cancelled, not every delay.

novel_features.name: Delay list
novel_features.description: List late trains at a station with delay minutes.
novel_features.rationale: Computes delay from planned vs changed timestamps after the overlay join.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for late-but-running trains; cancellations are a different command.

novel_features.name: Cheap change watch
novel_features.description: Apply the last two minutes of rchg onto a cached plan+fchg snapshot.
novel_features.rationale: Only works if a local snapshot exists; official docs tell clients to poll rchg after fchg, and no competitor CLI does that against SQLite.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to poll cheaply after board/fchg; do not use it as the first fetch.

narrative.headline: Official station boards: delay, platform, cancel — not a journey planner.
narrative.value_prop: A Go CLI for Deutsche Bahn's Marketplace Timetables API. Resolve a station, pull the hourly plan, overlay live changes, and keep a local slice so an agent can ask follow-ups without burning quota. This is not A to B, fares, or booking.
narrative.auth_narrative: Marketplace Anwendung credentials. Every request must send both headers: DB-Client-Id from DB_TIMETABLES_CLIENT_ID (or DB_CLIENT_ID) and DB-Api-Key from DB_TIMETABLES_API_KEY (or DB_API_KEY). Auth is configured only when both values are present. Create an Anwendung, subscribe it to Timetables, and export the two env vars. Do not commit keys.

quickstart.comment: Health check that works without hitting the API.
Resolve a name or EVA without spending a live call.
Show the live-board request (plan + fchg overlay) for Frankfurt Hbf.
Platform-change filter for the same station.

troubleshoots.fix: Export both DB_TIMETABLES_CLIENT_ID and DB_TIMETABLES_API_KEY. One header is not enough.

troubleshoots.symptom: empty station results for a German name with umlauts
troubleshoots.fix: Retry with EVA or DS100 (FF, 8000105). The official station pattern does not handle umlauts well.

troubleshoots.symptom: plan looks on time but the train is late
troubleshoots.fix: plan is static. Use board (plan+fchg overlay) or fchg.
Marketplace is about 60 calls/min. Cache plan (static) and poll rchg after one fchg via watch.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when the task is a station board: resolve EVA, show planned trains for an hour, overlay delays/platform/cancel, or poll recent changes. Prefer board for the live picture, platforms/cancellations/delays for filtered questions, and watch after a snapshot.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to plan an A to B journey or local-transit itinerary.
Do not use this CLI to quote fares or book tickets.
Do not use this CLI to scrape bahn.de or DB Navigator.
Do not use this CLI as a substitute for the official DB Navigator consumer app.
